title: rubus parviflorus f. lacera
intro: Rubus parviflorus f. lacera, commonly known as the Thimbleberry, is a fragrant and edible species of wild raspberry native to North America. The health benefits of Thimbleberry include its potential to reduce inflammation and improve cardiovascular health due to its rich content of antioxidants, vitamins, and minerals. The therapeutic actions of Thimbleberry are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and anthocyanins, displaying anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties. The bioactive constituents of Thimbleberry have been found to include ellagic acid, kaempferol, and quercetin, which may contribute to its potential health benefits.
